title: GOV-0012: a project's badf/ control plane is decorative -- nothing validates an instance
problem:
## Observed
Since BADF-WP-0021 (`369d67a`), `badf init` writes `AGENTS.md`, `badf/project.yaml`, `badf/state.json` and an init receipt into the target. Nothing reads them back. There is no command that checks an instance's documents against their schemas, no corroboration that `state.json` and the receipt agree with each other and with the instance's git history, no check that the pinned `framework_revision` is a commit this framework actually has, and no integrity over `badf/` in the project — the framework's lockfile covers the framework only. A hand-edited `state.json` claiming `G12 / APPROVED` is indistinguishable from a derived one.

## Expected
`badf_gate.py instance <path>` — deterministic, offline: the three documents parse and pass their schemas; ids, work package and commits agree across `project.yaml`, `state.json` and the receipt; `baseline_commit` exists in the instance and is an ancestor of its HEAD; `framework_revision` is a commit known to this framework; a per-instance `badf/lockfile.json` (written by init, same format as the framework's) corroborates every file under `badf/` plus a generated `AGENTS.md`; a preserved `AGENTS.md` that changed since baseline is reported, not refused (it is the project's file). Deny unless established; the framework itself is refused as an instance.

## Evidence
`grep -n '"instance"' scripts/badf_gate.py` → only the registry entry and WP record written by init; no reader. `ls <target>/badf` after init → `evidence/ project.yaml state.json` — no lockfile.

## Unknowns
Whether the receipt's `generated` digests must still match once governed state transitions exist (later WP). For now the instance lockfile is the current integrity and the receipt is the day-0 record; both are checked.

## Proposed work package
`BADF-WP-0022` — `instance <path>` subcommand; per-instance lockfile written by init and verified by `instance`; the framework's lock/verify parameterised by root and patterns so there is ONE lockfile implementation; tests in scratch instances only (no project is touched); mutation; post-merge simulation.
